newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - bonds ease from high.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - bonds ease from high.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices in late trade on Friday stood about one-quarter of a point higher, having trimmed gains achieved just after a payrolls report that disclosed some surprisingly softer numbers.

Traders said that the market's initial kick higher, which pushed municipal bonds up as much as one-half a point, after the payrolls data stemmed in part from short-covering in muncipal bond and Treasury bond futures, as well as relief that the gain in jobs only slightly exceded forecasts.
For January, the Labor Department said payrolls climbed 271,000, a bit higher than forecast a consensus forecast.
"I think the market was almost happy the number was within the range, give or take, it was sort of like, it wasn't bad, it wasn't brutal," a trader explained.

The market also focused keenly on the drop in average weekly hours to 34.1 from 34.8. Some of the euphoria over this finding was erroded, however, when participants realized the drop partly stemmed from unusually bad weather in regions.
At the end of the day, this left market sentiment about evenly divided between whether the Federal Reserve next month was likely to tighten monetary policy or leave rates unchanged, traders said.
Average earnings per hour only rose one cent to $12.06, indicating only modest inflationary pressures. The unemployment rate firmed one percentage point to 5.4 percent.

While bid-wanted lists were circulated, traders said the volume was not sufficient to exert much pressure on prices. And with only moderate supplies of new issues slated for next week's calender, which totals about $2.7 billion, prices should keep hold of their firmer tone, at least at the start of next week, they said.

"They're a couple of negotiated deals, nothing huge, and the competitive calender is kind of a joke, there's just not a whole lot, so probably there will be customers with a lot of money and not a lot of bonds. So we're going to hang in there," one said.

While the total of new bonds slated for sale adds up to about $1.1 billion more than this week's supply, there are only 48 competitive deals scheduled, totaling $886 million. Thirty-eight negotiated deals are expected, totaling $1.82 billion.

The top competitive deal is expected to be Thursday's $250 million Illinois sale. The top negotiated deal is expected to be a $264 million Harris County Health Facilities Development Authority, Texas, offering via Smith Barney Inc.
And the negotiated calender includes an $82 million sale of general obligation bonds by Hempstead, New York, on Friday.
March U.S. Treasury bond futures rose 11 ticks to 115-30/32, while the municipal bond futures climbed 18 ticks to 112-15/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 11 ticks.
In the secondary market, Denver Colorado City & County Airport Revenues of November 2025, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.78 percent, NET, down four basis points.

And Metropolitan Pier & Exposition Authority Illinois Dedicated State Tax Revenues of June 2027, which have a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.72 percent, down eight basis points. ((--Joan Gralla, 212-859-1654)) (c) Reuters Limited 1997
